newsitem.title: USA: CME approves board for CME's Depository Trust Co.
newsitem.headline: CME approves board for CME's Depository Trust Co.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) board last week approved seven directors to serve on the board of the CME-Depository Trust Company (DTC), the exchange said.

A CME spokesman said CME chairman Jack Sandner, CME president Rick Kilcollin, CME chairman emeritus Leo Melamed and board members Scott Gordon and Thomas Kloet will serve one-year terms on the DTC board.
Mark Brickell, managing director of J.P. Morgan Securities, and Cristobal Conde, chairman and CEO of SunGard Capital Markets, were approved to serve as outside directors.
Three other outside directors will be selected, with each heading either the DTC's Asian, European or Americas User Advisory committees, the spokesman said.
All outside directors will be paid a fee, which a CME spokesman would not disclose.
The launch date for DTC was changed to the second quarter, from the first quarter, he said. Last October, 11 financial institutions signed letters of intent to join DTC.
DTC, a subsidiary of the CME, will record and match privately negotiated derivatives transactions to reduce administrative and operational burdens on firms.
The DTC will also revalue and reset derivative transactions upon request from participating members.
The CME, SunGard Capital Markets and the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunications, will jointly run the DTC. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
